- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting periods when sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for 3–7 days to capture reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong upward momentum, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 7 days.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 2–4% for 3–5 days to avoid “sentiment-driven overbought” bias.
